Hi Jamie / Ops team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick written recap and two asks so we can lock the trial plan. High level: SaaSOps wants a 4-week trial that validates production latency/cost at 1) steady-state business traffic and 2) realistic burst scenarios during heavy user events. Below is the proposal we discussed.

Summary of proposed capacity & autoscaling
- Reserved baseline: 2 x A100 80GB (reserved for the trial window, dedicated to SaaSOps namespace)
- Autoscaling policy: allow burst up to 6 GPUs (same SKU) over short windows (10–30 minutes) for load spikes; burst will be subject to short-term billing; Redwood will enforce graceful fallback after sustained overload
- Canary / fallback: route to quantized / smaller model variant (e.g., MPT-30Q) when burst capacity unavailable; keep 1 replica of quantized variant warm for <100ms cold-start penalty
- Expected concurrency profile we measured in call: median 25 concurrent sessions, peak 180 concurrent requests (burst); target p95 latency goal during steady-state: <250ms per response generation (prompt + tokens)

Success criteria (how SaaSOps will evaluate)
- Latency: p50/p95 measured across the provided 50-prompt test set; steady-state p95 <250ms, burst p95 <500ms with graceful degraded quality acceptable
- Cost: token cost per 1k tokens and projected monthly run-rate not exceeding threshold in the MAP (see attachment)
- Functional: 90% pass-rate on the evaluation rubric (clarity, hallucination rate <= 5% on labeled prompts)
- Operational: rollout/rollback validated; autoscale triggers execute predictably and logs/traces available in Console

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0 (prep): May 24–31 — network setup, credentialing, and test dataset upload (SaaSOps to share sanitized prompt set by 5/26)
- Week 1 (kickoff): Jun 1 — trial goes live with baseline reserved GPUs, smoke tests + synthetic traffic
- Week 2: Jun 8 — real traffic ramp to steady-state targets; collect metrics
- Week 3: Jun 15 — burst day simulation (we’ll coordinate a window to drive peak load; Redwood will enable burst to 6 GPUs)
- Week 4 (wrap): Jun 22 — evaluation meeting, export of logs, decision/next steps

Ownership & next steps
- Jordan Blake (me): overall engagement lead, single point to coordinate scheduling and escalation
- Marissa Cole: customer success lead for onboarding, will run trial kickoff and acceptance testing
- Dev Patel: infra configuration owner — will provision reserved pool, autoscale policies, and network egress settings

Two asks for you this week (blockers to schedule):
1) Confirm you can accept a dedicated reserved pool for the 4-week window and who on your side signs the resource commitment (we need the name/email for the contract stub)
2) Share the sanitized evaluation prompt set by Wed 5/26 and a short list of 3 traffic windows where you want us to simulate peak load

Attachments: trial-success-criteria.xlsx (scoring rubric), mutual-action-plan.docx (MUTUAL ACTION PLAN with dates)

If that aligns, we’ll prepare the contract stub and spin up the reserved capacity on Jun 1 at 08:00 PDT.

Thanks — Jordan

Jamie — great questions, answered inline below.

1) Burst cap mechanics: the "6 GPUs" is a hard-configured burst ceiling for the trial environment (we will not auto-scale beyond 6 GPUs). If sustained load continues beyond 30 minutes and capacity is saturated, Redwood will: 1) execute graceful fallback (route traffic to quantized model variant), 2) emit an alert and 3) stop further autoscale upsizes until an operator acknowledges. Billing for the burst period is pro-rated; we’ll include an example bill in the MAP.

2) Billing / procurement: baseline reserved pool is billed pro-rata for the calendar month and treated as the trial minimum for the committed window. Cancellation: 7-day notice prior to the start of the reserved window (for this trial we can be flexible — we’ll honor a 48-hour cancellation if something critical comes up).

Extra detail on fallback: we’ll keep an MPT-30Q variant hot (single replica) to limit cold-start latency. Dev will instrument traces to show when fallbacks occur so you can map user-visible regressions.

If you confirm the reservation and share the contact for the resource-commitment signature, we’ll issue the stub contract and schedule Jun 1 provisioning.

Best — Jordan
